resolved.description: False when the path did not exist; say so rather than substituting another paper.

job.description: One sentence a writer could follow.

move.description: context | tension | gap | insight | built | contributions | result

exemplar.description: A quoted sentence from a reference paper; a rule without one is unusable.

reference_figure.description: Where it came from, e.g. 'gemm_sp_paper fig 5'.

banned.description: Constructions the reference papers never use, derived from reading them rather than from generic style advice.

reference_spec_path.description: The durable markdown spec later stages read as a file.

section_budget.job: Set the tension that the status quo cannot resolve, name the one insight, list contributions, show the headline number before §2.
Establish the template paradigm and its three failure dimensions; end able to say why each is fatal.
Present the grammar, then the compiler-harness co-design; every feature paired with its tuning impact.
State what is real, what is a shortcut, and the artifact layout.
Headline speedup, then per-operator spread, then ablations that isolate each contribution.
Position against template DSLs and autotuners by axis, not paper by paper.
Restate the claim at the level of generality it earned, then the open problem.

storyline_arc.how: Name a practice that everyone accepts and show its cost in the same sentence.
storyline_arc.exemplar: Kernel authors today re-state the same tiling decision once per operator, and pay for it in porting cost rather than in cycles.

storyline_arc.how: One sentence, no hedging, immediately after the gap.
storyline_arc.exemplar: The decision is the same in both cases; only the spelling differs, so the spelling is what a compiler should own.

storyline_arc.how: State what the closest prior work cannot deliver, on one named axis, so the boundary is checkable.
storyline_arc.exemplar: Templated libraries expose the decision but keep it per operator, so a new format still costs a new template.

storyline_arc.how: Three to four bullets, each naming the artifact that establishes it, never a promise about future sections.
storyline_arc.exemplar: We present a single operator grammar whose configurations reach within 8% of hand-tuned kernels on six sparse shapes.

rules: One bar per baseline library, grouped by operator; the fastest custom kernel is annotated with its numeric speedup.
A dashed horizontal line at 1.0 marks parity, never the fastest baseline.
The caption's first sentence states the claim; later sentences only tell the reader which axis to compare.
figure_grammar.caption_exemplar: Speedup over the released library for each operator. Bars above the dashed line are faster than cuBLAS; the annotated value is the best configuration found by the tuner.

openers: A subsection opens with the mechanism's consequence, not with what the subsection will discuss: "The check runs before the kernel, so a tiling error costs a message instead of a hang."
transitions: A section closes by naming the next section's precondition: "Those checks are cheap only if the compiler already knows the layout, which is what §3.3 provides."
claims: A result is stated with its measurement basis attached: "1.58x over the released baseline, measured over 240 shapes with the harness in §4.2."
banned: No 'In recent years' or 'With the rapid development of' openings.
No contribution stated without its validating artifact.
No figure reference without a reading instruction for the reader.
